speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing? How long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste you described is a very specific type of aura, which often originates from the temporal lobe. To help narrow this down, do you have any history of head injuries, high fevers, or seizures in your family?
